_comment_ignoreCommand: Exit 0 skips the build, exit 1 runs it. Three conditions must ALL hold
before a build is skipped: the commit has a single parent, its message is
one the agent wrote, and it touched nothing outside journal/.
The first condition is the one learned the hard way. Comparing HEAD^ to
HEAD on a MERGE compares against the first parent - the branch being
merged into - so a merge that brings in journal commits looks like a
journal-only change even when the local side carried code. A fix to
api/live.py was pushed that way and never deployed: the build was skipped
and the site kept serving the bug it fixed. Merges now always build.
The message check is the belt to that braces. Only scripts/commit_journal.sh
writes 'Journal: cycle ...', so anything a person or another tool commits
deploys no matter which files it touched.
ignoreCommand: if git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD^2 >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi; git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q '^Journal: cycle ' || exit 1; git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- . ':(exclude)journal' || exit 1; exit 0
